Q: Move time 1 hour back on range of rows in pandas A:

There are a few mistakes in your code.

  • You can't add a TimeDelta to a string (there is not "time" type in pandas, only "datetime")
  • You should avoid chained assignments like df.loc[mask]["Time"]

Create a mask with isin, convert the date+time to_datetime, subtract your Timedelta, and convert back to string with .dt.strftime:

mask = df['Date'].isin(['06.01.2026', '07.01.2026'])
dt = pd.to_datetime(df['Date']+' '+df['Time'], dayfirst=True)
corrected = dt[mask].sub(pd.Timedelta('1h'))
df.loc[mask, 'Time'] = corrected.dt.strftime('%H:%M')

Output:

         Date   Time
0  05.01.2026  17:00
1  06.01.2026  17:00
2  07.01.2026  17:00
3  08.01.2026  17:00

If you also want to change the date if the subtraction can get it to move to the previous day:

df.loc[mask, 'Date'] = corrected.dt.strftime('%d.%m.%Y')
